overview: This Senate resolution congratulates the students, families, teachers and leaders of public charter schools and supports the goals of the 26th National Charter Schools Week, May 11 through May 17, 2025. Charter schools are tuition-free public schools that run with more independence than traditional public schools but are held accountable by the organization that authorizes them. The resolution notes that about 3.7 million children attend roughly 8,000 charter schools, cites research finding learning gains for low-income charter students, and encourages communities to hold events supporting high-quality charter schools. The Senate approved it by unanimous consent on May 20, 2025.
for: Supporters say charter schools give families more public school choices and the resolution recognizes the educators and students who make them work.
against: Critics say the resolution does not change any law, and some argue it praises one type of school while charter schools can draw students and funding away from traditional public schools.
